title: Optimal Information and Concavification in Bayesian Persuasion
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz
summary: Kamenica and Gentzkow's finite-state persuasion theorem from economic primitives: nonempty compact metric actions, continuous sender and receiver utilities, and a full-support common prior. Receiver best replies and sender-preferred tie actions exist. The induced sender payoff is bounded and upper semicontinuous. Finite signals realize exactly finite Bayes-plausible posterior splittings, with prescribed posteriors recovered only at nonnull messages.
